newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco firms seek to block disclosure on content.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco firms seek to block disclosure on content.

text.p: Tobacco company lawyers will argue Wednesday in Boston's U.S. District Court that Massachusetts should not holding public hearings on regulations that would force the firms to disclose the contents of cigarettes, lawyers for the companies told Reuters.

The four firms challenging the regulations are: Philip Morris Cos Inc, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc and Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp.

The tobacco companies filed suit in federal court last August after Massachusetts Gov. William Weld signed into a law a bill that would force them to reveal the ingredients in each of their cigarette brands to the Department of Public Health, which has vowed to make those recipes known to consumers.
The department has scheduled public hearings on the proposed rules for Thursday and Friday and lawyers for the firms say the hearings themselves are a form of disclosure.
"The rulemaking process itself is a form of discovery," said lawyer David Remes, who represents the four firms.
